lesson_title: Exponent Laws: The Grammar of Algebra
hook_text: x to the MINUS 2 is not negative. It's not zero. It's hiding somewhere else.
clip_script: A negative exponent means reciprocal: x to the negative two is one over x squared — because subtracting exponents can drive the count below zero, and the x's keep cancelling into the denominator. A negative exponent is a position instruction — move to the other side of the fraction line — not a negative number. And anything nonzero to the power zero equals one — because x cubed divided by x cubed is both one and, by law two, x to the zero. The laws are not rules to memorise; they are consequences of what an exponent counts.
